programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: It's wildcard week, where we visit three escapes that don't fit into any of this year's categories but that our industry panel decided had to be included. Kirsty and Helen from Perthshire rate former farm Monachyle Mhor in the Trossachs, House of Gods hotel in Edinburgh, and Glen Dye, a 15,000-acre private estate in Aberdeenshire.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: When a woman crashes her mobility scooter down an embankment, paramedics are on hand to help. In Edinburgh, crewmates Kevin and Martyn treat an unconscious homeless patient.

programme.desc: Alan is laid up on the sofa after an accident. Beth and Eric are looking after him when Christine arrives with goodies, and Colin can't wait to share details of internet dates.

programme.title: Situationships with Sophie and Christine
programme.desc: Sharing some of their worst dating experiences, Sophie and Christine bring the laughs as they discuss everything from pant sniffing fetishes to ghosting to witnessing an unexpected sex show. The pair also discuss latest drama from the celeb world.

programme.title: Situationships with Sophie and Christine
programme.desc: The audiences will be taken on a rollercoaster ride of funny, bizarre, and downright weird stories of when relationships take an unexpected turn. Witnessing listeners' dating dilemmas, relationship revelations, and situationship struggles.

programme.desc: Tracing the history of linoleum to its origins in the mid 19th century and examining how the Scottish port town of Kirkcaldy become the world centre for its manufacture. programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: Brian Low is shot and found dead in rural Scotland. Now, David Campbell, former gamekeeper of the shooting estate where he worked, stands accused of his premeditated murder.

programme.title: The Fringe, Fame and Me
programme.desc: Told by the stars who first found fame at the Edinburgh Fringe, this is the inside story of what it takes to make a name here, from those who enjoyed overnight success, to those who slogged for years to make it. Through their triumphs, favourite jokes and sometimes painful failures, discover a hidden history of British comedy, revealing how the gags we find funny and the comedians we love reflect our changing culture.

programme.desc: Jules and Greg are in Glasgow and Edinburgh, exploring Scotland's urban cold-water locations.
